title: A1-03 · Male and female, concordance of the adjective

blocks.text: A1-03 · Male and female, concordance of the adjective
Lesson overview

Each Arabic name is masculine or feminine, and the adjective follows: ⁧مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ A big city. ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ It's a big house. This unity teaches you to recognize gender, to form feminine and to describe people, places and objects. It lasts two weeks: the first for the rules, the second to enlarge the descriptive vocabulary and write the first descriptions.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 15–16 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-03), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the kind of a name by form and know the female without ⁧ة⁩ more frequent;
2. to form the female adjectives and professional names;
3. put the adjective after the name and accord it in the genre, even with two adjectives;
4. Use the adjective as a predicate ( ⁧هِيَ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ ) and strengthen it with ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ;
5. describe two people and one city in 40 words;
6. recognize when listening if you talk about a man or a woman.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: . ⁧هِيَ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ ! ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: mā šāʾa llāh! hiya ǧamīla. Luke: How beautiful, God bless you! It's beautiful.

What to notice. ⁧مَنْ⁩ You'll study it in A1-06: here is a fixed block. ⁧صَغِيرٌ⁩ the name of the brother means "young" or "little girl." ⁧أُمِّي⁩ , ⁧أَخِي⁩ , ⁧بِنْتِي⁩ have the suffix -ī Mine/my. Luca uses ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ ( A1-01) to compliment the child: it is the usual way of praising a child without attracting the evil eye, an attention widespread in many Arab families.
2. The kind of names
In Arabic there is no neutral: every name is male ( ⁧مُذَكَّر⁩ muḏakkar ) or female ( ⁧مُؤَنَّث⁩ muʾannaṯ ). Male does not have a particular sign; women, in the vast majority of cases, end up ⁧ة⁩ .
⁧سَيَّارَةمَكْتَب⁩ office · automobile

The rule of thumb. A word that ends in ⁧ة⁩ is female; a word without ⁧ة⁩ is male, except for the exceptions of the section 3. The kind of things doesn't coincide with Italian: ⁧كِتَاب⁩ Book is male as in English, but ⁧شَمْس⁩ is female; and ⁧حَرْب⁩ It's also war.
3. Female without ⁧ة⁩ and male with ⁧ة⁩
They are a few words, but very frequent. Learn them by their kind.
Women for ⁧أُمّ⁩ ummm madre · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint girl, daughter · ⁧أُخْت⁩ The meaning is feminine: ⁧ة⁩ no nature is needed uḫt sister

rows: ⁧شَمْس⁩ šams sun · ⁧أَرْض⁩ arḍ soil · ⁧حَرْب⁩ ḥarb war · ⁧دَار⁩ dār home, seat · ⁧نَار⁩ nār fire
They should be stored (in Anki they are marked "f."
Almost all parts of the body that are in pairs are female
Place names are usually female; exceptions: ⁧المَغْرِب⁩ , ⁧العِرَاق⁩ , ⁧لُبْنَان⁩ , ⁧السُّودَان⁩ , ⁧الأُرْدُنّ⁩

blocks.text: Men with ⁧حَمْزَةة⁩ Ḥamza · ⁧أُسَامَة⁩ Usāma · ⁧خَلِيفَة⁩ ḫalīfa The meaning is masculine: the agreement is masculine caliph ( ⁧حَمْزَة طَالِبٌ⁩ )
Because you need it. In reading their own names, in A2, you'll see ⁧حَمْزَة⁩ and ⁧أُسَامَة⁩ are common male names: do not attribute them to a woman for ⁧ة⁩ Final.
4. Forming the Female
For adjectives and person names you add ⁧ة⁩ to the male. In front of the ⁧ة⁩ the last consonant takes the fatḥa.
Attention to the words in -iyy and the šadda. In ⁧مُهِمّ⁩ and ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ the šadda remains and the fatḥa go over the double letter:

Exception to recognize. The adjectives of color and physical defect have a different feminine: ⁧أَحْمَر⁩ aḥmar Red-red → ⁧حَمْرَاء⁩ ḥamrāʾ . You will study them in A2; For now know that they exist. The ⁧ة⁩ paused and connected. In pause we read -a ( ⁧كَبِيرَة⁩ kabīra ); Inside the sentence one reads -at more desinence ( ⁧كَبِيرَةٌ جِدًّا⁩ kabīratun ǧiddan ).
5. The Adjective's Agreement
Attributional adjective. It follows the name, always, and takes its kind (and desinence, which here is -a):
⁧حَرْبٌ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ ḥarbun ṭawīla a long war ( ⁧حَرْب⁩ is female)
Predicted adjective. After a pronoun or proper name, the adjective itself forms the nominal phrase (A1-02):

Because the adjective goes later. In Arabic the name comes first and what qualifies it follows: it is a fixed order, not stylistic. Beautiful city with the adjective in front ( ⁧جَمِيلَةٌ مَدِينَةٌ⁩ ) is not an Arabic phrase.
6. Two adjectives, ⁧جِدًّا⁩ and ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩

More adjectives are put one after the other, all agreed: ⁧مَدِينَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ It is an ancient and beautiful city. As preached they bind with ⁧وَ⁩ : ⁧القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ وَقَدِيمَةٌ⁩ . ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ǧiddan "Much" goes after the adjective: ⁧كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا⁩ Very big. It doesn't change for the genre. ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ lākin "but" combines two sentences: . ⁧البَيْتُ صَغِيرٌ، لٰكِنْ هُوَ جَمِيلٌ⁩ In front of the article he took the support: ⁧لٰكِنِ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ⁩ lākini l-ǧawwu bārid It's cold, though. The ā of ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ is written with the short alif (L0-09). ⁧أَوْ⁩ aw .o., or ⁧طَوِيلٌ أَوْ قَصِيرٌ؟⁩ High or low?

blocks.text: What to notice. The cities are feminine: ⁧القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ , ⁧مِيلَانُو صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ . ⁧النِّيل⁩ is male: . ⁧طَوِيلٌ⁩ In ⁧النِّيلُ⁩ and ⁧الجَوُّ⁩ the article gives a name determined as subject: it is the structure of A1-04.
8. Pronunciation

⁧ة⁩ Inside the sentence. madīnatun kabīra : ⁧ة⁩ It is pronounced t when it follows desinence. Read madīna kabīra Inside a formal sentence is a reading error (acceptable only in the quick talk). Doubles. ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧حَارٌّ⁩ , ⁧مُهِمٌّ⁩ , ⁧جَيِّدٌ⁩ have the šadda: Keep the consonant twice as much as in English. ǧidan instead of ǧiddan It's a frequent mistake. ⁧ص⁩ and ⁧س⁩ . ⁧صَغِير⁩ ṣaġīr starts with ṣād emphasis: the following is dark, almost [ɑ]. ⁧سَعِيد⁩ saʿīd starts with sīn simple and has a ʿayn In the middle. ⁧غ⁩ in ⁧صَغِير⁩ . It is the airy/uvular sound fricativa of L0-07, not a g and not an Italian r.

Notes of use. ⁧اِمْرَأَة⁩ loses the initial aliif with the article: ⁧المَرْأَة⁩ al-marʾa . ⁧كَبِير⁩ said of a person often means "older" ( ⁧كَبِيرٌ فِي السِّنِّ⁩ kabīrun fī s-sinn \n years before the end of the period; ⁧صَغِير⁩ Young. ⁧طَوِيل⁩ and ⁧قَصِير⁩ apply to things (long, short) and people (high, low). The plural of ⁧أَرْض⁩ , ⁧أَرَاضٍ⁩ , has a particular shape that you will see in B1.

13. Writing

Week 1: describe two people (a woman and a man) with three sentences each: work, an adjective for appearance, an adjective for character. Week 2: extends the text to about 40 words adding the city in which they live, with two adjectives and ⁧جِدًّا⁩ . Use at least once ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ .
